compared.difference: That item counts the flattening lemma (Theorem 6.12.2, source hits.tex lines 1833-1836) with retained proof ranges 1772-1785 and 1838-2039. Its retained ranges consume the neighbouring flattening variants but do not contain hits.tex lines 933-1009, so the pushout universal property was not counted there. The flattening lemma is about a type family over a pushout; the present lemma is the universal property of the pushout itself, which the flattening lemma only cites.

compared.difference: Searches of reference/public-items.jsonl with the object names returned only unrelated near neighbours: 465 and 491 (pushouts of scheme thickenings along affine morphisms exist as schemes), 495 (pushout descent of objects of an algebraic stack) and 736 (pseudo-coherent derived triples glue across affine pushouts). Those are statements in algebraic geometry about schemes and stacks, with no cocone, no function-type equivalence and no higher inductive type.
